successCriteria.description: The LeaveRequest entity is defined and exported from the leave module's model file, with its `status` field typed as `LeaveStatus` imported from `shared/types` — a reviewer can verify the import source and that the type is not a free string.

The ILeaveRepository interface is defined and exported with all six operations (findById, findByEmployeeId, findByStatus, create, update, updateStatus), each declaring the correct return type (LeaveRequest | null for single-row reads/updates, LeaveRequest[] for list reads, LeaveRequest for create).
The LeaveRepository class implements ILeaveRepository and compiles under strict TypeScript with zero `any` types — `tsc --noEmit` / `npm run build` passes for the new files.
findById returns null (not undefined, not a throw) when no row matches the given id; it returns a fully mapped LeaveRequest when a row exists.
create persists a new leave_requests row via INSERT ... RETURNING * and returns the mapped LeaveRequest entity (including server-generated id, createdAt, updatedAt).

updateStatus sets approved_at to NOW() when the target status is APPROVED; for non-APPROVED statuses it does not set approved_at to now. The method returns the updated LeaveRequest or null when the row does not exist.

findByEmployeeId builds a dynamic WHERE clause from LeaveRequestQueryParams (status, policyId, startDateFrom/To, endDateFrom/To) using parameterized placeholders, appends LIMIT/OFFSET only when provided, and returns the mapped LeaveRequest[] — an empty result yields an empty array, never null.

update builds a dynamic SET clause only for provided fields and falls back to findById (returning the current row) when no updatable fields are supplied; it returns null when the target row does not exist.
The barrel index.ts re-exports LeaveRequest and ILeaveRepository from the model file and LeaveRepository from the repository file, so consumers can import all three from the module root.

Jest unit tests exist at tests/unit/modules/leave/ (ending in .test.ts), mock the pool from shared/db/connection, and assert both the returned mapped entity values and the exact SQL string + params array passed to pool.query for each repository method.
The full verification command (npm install + npm run build + npx jest --passWithNoTests) exits zero with the new leave module files and tests present.

constraints: All database access must go through the repository layer (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository, severity critical): the LeaveRepository is the only component that issues SQL against the leave_requests table; no inline SQL or direct pool usage outside the repository file.
No `any` type anywhere in the new files (HARNESS no-any, severity high): use `Record<string, unknown>` for row shapes and `unknown[]` for parameter arrays, with type assertions at mapping boundaries.
Strict TypeScript must pass (tsconfig strict: true, no implicit any, strict null checks) — the new files must compile cleanly under `npm run build` / `tsc --noEmit`.
All SQL must use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, …) — no string interpolation of user-supplied values into query text (SQL-injection prevention; matches employee/policy repo convention).

Modules import from sibling modules only through their declared public entry point (index.ts) — the leave module must not import employee/policy internals directly; Employee and LeavePolicy are type references only and are not imported into the model file per the task spec.

Test files must end in `.test.ts` and be placed under `tests/unit/modules/leave/` to match the jest testMatch glob (`**/tests/**/*.test.(ts|js)`); imports use path aliases resolvable via moduleDirectories (`modules/...`, `shared/db/connection`, `shared/types`).

The `leave_type` column exists in the leave_requests table but is NOT part of the LeaveRequest entity surface — the repository must not expose it as an entity field; it may be ignored on read and omitted on write unless required by the schema.
outOfScope: Leave service, controller, and routes (Phases 9–10) — no ILeaveService, LeaveService, LeaveController, or leaveRoutes in this phase.
Business-rule validation (employee ACTIVE, policy ACTIVE, balance sufficiency, minimum notice, date-range checks) — that logic belongs to the service layer in Phase 9, not the repository.
Balance deduction/restoration, audit logging, and notification dispatch — these are cross-module orchestrations in Phase 9; the repository only persists/reads LeaveRequest rows.
HTTP layer, RBAC middleware, and input validation at API boundaries (GP-003/GP-005) — deferred to the controller/routes phase.
Database migrations or schema DDL for the leave_requests table — the schema is pre-declared in the reconciled architecture; this phase assumes the table exists.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeaveRequest's status is always one of the LeaveStatus values (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED); the repository must never persist or return a status outside this set, and the entity's status field is typed as LeaveStatus (not a free string).

approvedAt is non-null only when the request has been approved (status APPROVED with approvedBy set); the updateStatus operation enforces this by setting approved_at = NOW() exclusively on the APPROVED transition. A request that is DRAFT/SUBMITTED/REJECTED/CANCELLED has approvedAt = null.

rejectionReason is non-null only for REJECTED requests; approvedBy is non-null only for APPROVED requests. The repository preserves these nullability relationships when mapping rows and when updating status.

Every persisted LeaveRequest has server-generated id, createdAt, and updatedAt (the create operation omits these from its input type via Omit and relies on INSERT ... RETURNING * to populate them); a caller cannot supply id/createdAt/updatedAt through the create signature.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no row matches the id (not undefined, not a thrown error); returns a fully mapped LeaveRequest when found.
Returns an empty array (never null) when no rows match; applies optional LeaveRequestQueryParams filters as a dynamic WHERE clause with LIMIT/OFFSET.
Returns an empty array (never null) when no rows match the given LeaveStatus.
Persists via INSERT ... RETURNING * and returns the mapped LeaveRequest with server-generated id/createdAt/updatedAt; input type excludes id/createdAt/updatedAt via Omit.
Returns null when the target row does not exist; falls back to findById (returning the current row) when no updatable fields are supplied; builds a dynamic SET clause only for provided fields.
Returns null when the target row does not exist; sets approved_at = NOW() when status is APPROVED (and persists approvedBy); does not set approved_at to now for non-APPROVED statuses.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeaveRepository must replicate the established repository pattern from EmployeeRepository: module-level `pool` import from `../../shared/db/connection`, parameterized SQL ($1, $2, …), a private `mapRow` helper converting snake_case columns to camelCase entity fields, `findById` returning null on empty rows, `create` using INSERT ... RETURNING *, and `update` building a dynamic SET clause via a fieldMap with findById fallback when no fields are supplied.

The LeaveRepository's update method must follow the same dynamic-SET + fieldMap + `updated_at = NOW()` + findById-fallback structure used by PolicyRepository, so the three repositories are structurally consistent.

The LeaveRequest entity's `status` field and the ILeaveRepository method signatures must import and use LeaveStatus (and LeaveRequestQueryParams) from `shared/types` rather than redefining them, preserving the single source of truth for these types established in Phase 1.

The leave barrel index.ts must follow the same export shape as the employee/policy barrels: re-export the entity interface and the repository interface from the model file, and re-export the repository class from the repository file.

The leave repository tests must follow the established test conventions: jest.mock('shared/db/connection', () => ({ pool: { query: jest.fn() } })), a snake_case makeRow(overrides) fixture helper, mockQuery.mockReset() in beforeEach, and assertions on both mapped return values and the exact SQL string + params array passed to pool.query.

The repository's column mapping must match the reconciled leave_requests schema (id, employee_id, policy_id, leave_type, start_date, end_date, status, reason, rejection_reason, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at), mapping camelCase entity fields to these snake_case columns; the leave_type column is present in the schema but excluded from the LeaveRequest entity surface per the task spec.

integrationPoints.why: Provides LeaveStatus, LeaveRequestQueryParams, CreateLeaveRequestDto, and UpdateLeaveRequestDto — the leave model imports LeaveStatus for the entity's status field and LeaveRequestQueryParams for the findByEmployeeId signature.
Provides the pg Pool instance the LeaveRepository imports at module level to execute parameterized queries against the leave_requests table.
Employee is a type reference for the leave_requests.employee_id and leave_requests.approved_by foreign keys; referenced as a type only (no runtime import in the model per task spec).
LeavePolicy is a type reference for the leave_requests.policy_id foreign key; referenced as a type only (no runtime import in the model per task spec).

The ILeaveRepository interface and LeaveRepository implementation produced in this phase are the persistence contract the future LeaveService will depend on for submit/approve/reject/cancel orchestration; the interface signatures must remain stable for that consumer.
